title: Wilson disease
everyday_terms: liver problems in a young person
summary: Wilson disease means the body cannot get rid of extra copper. Copper builds up, mainly in the liver and the brain, and signs often start in childhood or young adulthood.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the ATP7B gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has Wilson disease. It is treatable: lifelong treatment from a specialist team removes extra copper, and starting early helps prevent damage.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has Wilson disease. Could I be a carrier?
Can Wilson disease skip a generation?
What does a test for the ATP7B gene involve?
card_summary: Extra copper builds up in the liver and brain. It is treatable. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Copper builds up; lifelong treatment from a specialist team.
care: Specialist liver and neurology clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
